property_summary: C.transfer always reverts when _tos is empty (require(_tos.length > 0)) and returns true otherwise; the empty-input revert is the tested rule.
C.transfer returns true whenever _tos is non-empty, and its low-level call success forces no revert on any array element.
For a single-recipient transfer whose token low-level call succeeds, C.transfer always returns true and does not revert.
If the token contract rejects every transferFrom call, C.transfer must itself revert (propagating the failure) rather than return true.
For any nonempty recipient list and any value, C.transfer never reverts and always returns true (inner transferFrom failures are ignored via low-level calls).
C.transfer always reverts when the recipient list is empty.
For any nonempty recipient list and any value, calling C.transfer with a token address that has no code succeeds and returns true (low-level call to a codeless address returns success).
A call to C.transfer never moves Ether: address(c).balance remains 0 after the call, which returns true for a nonempty recipient list.
C.transfer is not payable, so any call carrying Ether always reverts, regardless of the arguments.
Calling C.transfer with an empty _tos array always reverts, while a non-empty array returns true (provided the external transferFrom succeeds).
